question: Uterine atony — failure of the myometrium to contract and retract after placental delivery — accounts for approximately 80% of all cases of postpartum haemorrhage.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Uterine atony is by far the most common cause of PPH, responsible for approximately 80% of cases. The remaining 20% are due to trauma, retained tissue, and coagulopathy (the 4 Ts).
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Uterine atony is the most common cause of PPH (~80%), which is why all initial management algorithms prioritise uterine massage, bimanual compression, and uterotonic drugs before investigating other causes.
